mainTopic: The כהן גדול and יבום, mourning and comforting; and why some kings are not judged (the story of ינאי)
overview: The amud opens by finishing the reason a כהן גדול cannot do יבום. A widow from נישואין is forbidden to him by both a לא תעשה and an עשה. A widow from אירוסין would be allowed by Torah law, but the חכמים forbade even the first ביאה because of the second, and a ברייתא backs this up. Next, the גמרא explains how a mourning כהן גדול may follow a relative's funeral: only from a distance, out of sight of the procession. It then explains why רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה argue over whether he may go as far as the city gate. A ברייתא sets out who stands beside the כהן גדול when he comforts mourners and when he is comforted, and רב פפא learns three lessons from it. The גמרא also tells how the order of comforting mourners was changed in ירושלים and changed back by רבי יוסי in ציפורי, along with two other תקנות of his and the rule that a comforters' line needs ten people. It settles that the כהן גדול says 'תתנחמו' when he comforts others. Finally, רב יוסף limits the rule that a king neither judges nor is judged to kings not from בית דוד, and the גמרא begins the story of ינאי המלך and שמעון בן שטח, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A married widow is forbidden by both a prohibition and a positive command
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא finishes its answer: an עשה cannot override a case that has both a לא תעשה and an עשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And a positive command does not override a prohibition that also comes with a positive command.
steps.whatsHappening: This is the last line of an answer that began just before here. It explains why a כהן גדול cannot do יבום with a widow who was fully married to his brother.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Such a widow is forbidden to a כהן גדול by a לא תעשה (no widow) and also by an עשה (he must marry a virgin, and she is a בעולה). The עשה of יבום is strong enough to push aside a single לא תעשה, but not a לא תעשה paired with an עשה.

keyTerms.meaning: A positive command, a מצוה to do something
A prohibition, a מצוה not to do something
A woman who is no longer a virgin

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule, that an עשה overrides a plain לא תעשה but not a לא תעשה together with an עשה, comes up all over ש״ס.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה.
phrases.english: And a positive command does not override a prohibition plus a positive command.
phrases.notes: The command to do יבום can't beat the pair of 'no widow' plus 'marry a virgin' together.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֵין עֲשֵׂה דּוֹחֶה לֹא תַעֲשֶׂה וַעֲשֵׂה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes the answer from just before here about a widow from נישואין.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limits the overriding power of an עשה
steps.terutzHavaAmina: We might think the עשה of יבום always overrides the prohibition on a כהן גדול marrying a widow.
steps.terutzMaskana: From נישואין there are two prohibitions (a לא תעשה and an עשה), so the עשה of יבום cannot override them.

steps.title: Then why not allow יבום when she was only engaged?
steps.stepSummary: If she was only engaged, she is still a virgin, so only one לא תעשה applies. The עשה of יבום should override it.
steps.simpleTranslation: But if she was only engaged, why not? Let the positive command come and override the prohibition!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer it just gave. That answer works for a married widow, but not for one who was only engaged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A woman widowed from אירוסין is still a virgin, so the עשה of 'marry a virgin' does not apply. Only the single לא תעשה of 'no widow' is left, and an עשה normally overrides a single לא תעשה. So why does the משנה forbid יבום in every case?

keyTerms.meaning: Engagement, the first stage of marriage before living together

phrases.english: But from betrothal, why not?
phrases.notes: He means a widow whose husband died while they were only engaged, so she is still a virgin.

phrases.english: Let the positive command come and override the prohibition!

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מִן הָאֵירוּסִין אַמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the reach of the answer in step 1.
steps.kashyaTarget: The משנה's blanket rule that a כהן גדול never does יבום
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The 'two prohibitions' answer only covers a widow from נישואין. From אירוסין there is only one לא תעשה, which an עשה should override.

steps.title: A rabbinic decree: the first act is forbidden because of the second
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים forbade even the first ביאה, because the couple might go on to a second ביאה that is not a מצוה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It is a decree: the first act of intercourse is forbidden because of the second act of intercourse.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. Strictly by Torah law the first ביאה would be allowed, but the חכמים made a גזירה against it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the first ביאה fulfills the מצוה of יבום, so only it can override the לא תעשה. Every later ביאה is not a מצוה and stays fully forbidden. Since the couple would probably go on living together, the חכמים forbade the first ביאה too.

keyTerms.meaning: A rabbinic decree made to protect against breaking a Torah law
Because of, out of concern for

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא does not say the Torah forbids this יבום. By Torah law the first ביאה would be allowed; the ban comes from the חכמים.

phrases.english: It is a decree on the first act of intercourse,
because of the second act of intercourse.

steps.triggerLanguage: גְּזֵירָה בִּיאָה רִאשׁוֹנָה אַטּוּ בִּיאָה שְׁנִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 2.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: From אירוסין, the עשה of יבום should override the single לא תעשה and allow it.
steps.terutzMaskana: By Torah law the first ביאה would be allowed, but the חכמים forbade it out of concern for a second, forbidden ביאה.

steps.title: A ברייתא supports the decree
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא says that if they went ahead with a first ביאה, the marriage takes effect, but they may not stay together for a second ביאה.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is also taught in a ברייתא: If they went ahead and had a first act of intercourse, they acquired her, but it is forbidden to keep them married for a second act.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that matches its answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא shows both sides of the answer. The first ביאה works, since it is a מצוה that overrides the לא תעשה, so the יבום takes effect. But they must not stay married, because any second ביאה is forbidden. That is the very concern behind the גזירה.

keyTerms.meaning: It was also taught this way (a ברייתא supports this)
They went ahead, did it before asking
To keep them (as husband and wife)

steps.whatToRemember: A כהן גדול may not do יבום even with an engaged widow. By Torah law the first ביאה would be allowed, but the חכמים forbade it because a second ביאה is truly forbidden. If he did it anyway, the יבום takes effect, but he may not stay married to her.

phrases.english: This is also taught in a baraita:
If they went ahead and had a first act of intercourse,
phrases.notes: The plural covers the כהן גדול and anyone else whose יבמה is forbidden to him.

phrases.english: they acquired her,
but it is forbidden to keep them married for a second act.

steps.triggerLanguage: תַּנְיָא נָמֵי הָכִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the answer of step 3.
steps.raayaObject: The difference between a first ביאה (allowed by Torah law, acquires) and a second ביאה (forbidden)

steps.title: The כהן גדול may follow a funeral, but not walk with it
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא turns to the משנה's line about a relative of the כהן גדול who died. A ברייתא reads the פסוק as forbidding him to go out with the procession, but allowing him to go after it.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'If a relative of his died...' The Rabbis taught: 'And from the Temple he shall not go out' means he may not go out with them, but he may go out after them.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic starts. The גמרא quotes the משנה and brings a ברייתא explaining the פסוק about the כהן גדול leaving the מקדש.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק seems to say the כהן גדול may not leave the מקדש at all for a funeral. The ברייתא reads it more narrowly: he may not walk together with the people escorting the מיטה, but following behind them is allowed.

phrases.english: If a relative of his died, etc.
The Rabbis taught:
'And from the Temple he shall not go out' —
he shall not go out with them,
but he goes out after them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מֵת לוֹ מֵת כּוּ׳ תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic from the משנה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The כהן גדול may not walk with the funeral procession, but he may follow after it.

steps.title: How does 'after them' work?
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks how the כהן גדול can follow without being together with the procession.
steps.simpleTranslation: How so?
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא asks a short question to set up its explanation of what 'after them' means in practice.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'After them' is unclear. How far behind must he be? The question asks for the exact practical picture.

phrases.english: How so?

steps.triggerLanguage: כֵּיצַד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks how to apply the rule of step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The practical meaning of following 'after them'

steps.title: He appears only when they are out of sight
steps.stepSummary: When the procession turns out of view, the כהן גדול comes into view, and when they come into view, he is hidden.
steps.simpleTranslation: When they are hidden, he is revealed; when they are revealed, he is hidden.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers: he follows at a distance, so that he and the procession are never seen at the same time.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the procession turns onto another street and disappears, he steps onto the street they just left. He stays one step behind and out of sight. This way he honors his relative but is never part of the procession itself.
steps.whatToRemember: The כהן גדול may follow a relative's funeral only from a distance, staying out of sight of the procession the whole time.

phrases.english: When they are hidden, he is revealed,
phrases.notes: Picture the procession turning a corner; only then does he step onto the street they left.

phrases.english: when they are revealed, he is hidden.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵן נִכְסִין וְהוּא נִגְלֶה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 6.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He follows at a distance so that he and the procession are never in view at the same time.

steps.title: רבי יהודה's view fits the verse well
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words about the כהן גדול going out until the city gate (רבי מאיר), and says that רבי יהודה, who says he does not leave the מקדש at all, reads the פסוק well.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'And he goes out until the entrance, etc.' רבי יהודה is saying it well.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a line from the משנה and says that רבי יהודה's view fits the פסוק 'from the מקדש he shall not go out.' This sets up a quiet challenge to רבי מאיר, which the next step answers.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר lets the כהן גדול walk after the procession until the city gate. רבי יהודה says he does not leave the מקדש at all. The plain words of the פסוק seem to back רבי יהודה, so רבי מאיר now needs an explanation.

keyTerms.meaning: Entrance; here, the gate of the city
He is saying it well; his view makes good sense
Etc.; the rest of the quote from the משנה

phrases.english: And he goes out until the entrance, etc.
phrases.notes: This is רבי מאיר's line in the משנה: the כהן גדול may follow the procession up to the city gate.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda is saying well.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁפִּיר קָאָמַר רַבִּי יְהוּדָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on from how the כהן גדול follows the procession (Step 7) to the משנה's argument over how far he may go.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי מאיר's ruling that the כהן גדול may go out until the city gate
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק says 'from the מקדש he shall not go out,' which fits רבי יהודה's view that he stays in the מקדש.

steps.title: רבי מאיר reads the verse as 'do not leave your holiness'
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר answers that if the פסוק were read literally, the כהן גדול could not even go home. So it must mean he should not leave his holiness by becoming טמא, and the gap between him and the procession protects him from touching the coffin.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר could tell you: If so, he should not even go to his house! Rather, this is what the פסוק means: 'From the מקדש he shall not go out' means 'from his holiness he shall not go out.' And since he has a clear sign that sets him apart, he will not come to touch the coffin.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי מאיר defends himself by showing that the literal reading cannot be right. He gives a different reading of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Everyone agrees the כהן גדול goes home, so 'do not leave the מקדש' cannot be meant literally. רבי מאיר reads מקדש as קדושה, meaning do not become טמא. Because the כהן גדול walks apart from the procession, that sign is enough to keep him from touching the coffin.

keyTerms.meaning: If so; if you read it that way
A clear sign or reminder that sets him apart

steps.confusionAlert: רבי מאיר is not saying the כהן גדול may leave the מקדש forever. He is saying the פסוק is about keeping his holiness (not becoming טמא), not about staying inside a building.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir could say to you:
If so, he should not go to his house either!
Rather, this is what it is saying:
"From the Temple he shall not go out"
From his holiness he shall not go out.
And since he has a recognizable sign,
he will not come to touch.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לָךְ רַבִּי מֵאִיר: אִי הָכִי, לְבֵיתוֹ נָמֵי לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from Step 8 on רבי מאיר's behalf.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Re-reading the פסוק (מקדש read as קדושה), backed by a reductio: read literally, he could not even go home.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק means the כהן גדול must stay in the מקדש building, which supports רבי יהודה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק means he must not become טמא. Walking apart from the procession is enough of a safeguard, so he may follow until the gate.

steps.title: רבי יהודה fears grief may lead him to touch
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה replies that the sign is not enough. In his grief, the כהן גדול might end up touching the coffin.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how would רבי יהודה answer? Because of his bitterness, it might happen that he comes and touches the coffin.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה would answer רבי מאיר and gives his reply: a grieving person may not stay careful.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר said walking apart is enough to keep him from touching. רבי יהודה says that strong grief can make a person forget himself, so a bigger separation is needed. That is why he keeps the כהן גדול in the מקדש.

keyTerms.meaning: It happens; it may come about

steps.whatToRemember: Both agree the goal is to keep the כהן גדול from becoming טמא. They only argue whether walking apart (רבי מאיר) is enough, or whether grief calls for staying in the מקדש (רבי יהודה).

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda?
Because of his bitterness,
perhaps it will happen that he comes and touches.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה: אַגַּב מְרָרֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's reply to רבי מאיר's reasoning in Step 9.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: Rejects רבי מאיר's claim that walking apart is a good enough safeguard
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: A grieving relative may lose control and touch the coffin anyway, so the sign is not reliable.

steps.title: Who stands beside the כהן גדול when comforting and being comforted
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the משנה's words 'when he comforts' and brings a ברייתא that spells out who stands on the כהן גדול's right and left, both when he comforts others and when others comfort him.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'When he comforts.' The רבנן taught: When the כהן גדול passes along the line to comfort others, the סגן and the former כהן גדול are on his right, and the ראש בית אב, the mourners, and all the people are on his left. When he stands in the line and is comforted by others, the סגן is on his right, and the ראש בית אב and all the people are on his left.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new line in the משנה about the כהן גדול comforting mourners. It brings a ברייתא with more detail about how the people around him are arranged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא gives two cases. When he comforts others, the סגן and the משוח שעבר are on his right, and the ראש בית אב, the mourners, and the people are on his left. When he is the mourner, only the סגן is on his right, and the משוח שעבר and the mourners are not mentioned.

keyTerms.meaning: Line or row of people at a comforting
A former כהן גדול who served for a time and then stepped down
Head of the כהנים family group serving in the מקדש that day

phrases.english: When he comforts.
The Rabbis taught:
When he passes along the line
to comfort others,
the deputy and the anointed one who has passed are on his right,
phrases.notes: 'The anointed one who has passed' is a former כהן גדול who filled in for a time and then stepped down.

phrases.aramaic: וְרֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב וַאֲבֵלִים וְכׇל הָעָם מִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ.
phrases.english: and the head of the father's house, the mourners, and all the people are on his left.
And when he stands in the line
and is comforted by others,
the deputy is on his right,

phrases.aramaic: וְרֹאשׁ בֵּית אָב וְכׇל הָעָם מִשְּׂמֹאלוֹ.
phrases.english: and the head of the father's house and all the people are on his left.

steps.triggerLanguage: כְּשֶׁהוּא מְנַחֵם. תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Leaves the funeral-procession argument and turns to the next line of the משנה, about comforting mourners.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the כהן גדול comforts others, the סגן and the משוח שעבר stand on his right, and the ראש בית אב, the mourners, and the people stand on his left. When he is comforted, the סגן is on his right, and the ראש בית אב and the people are on his left.

steps.title: The משוח שעבר does not come to comfort him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא notes what the ברייתא leaves out. When others comfort the כהן גדול, the former כהן גדול (משוח שעבר) is not among them.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the משוח שעבר (the former כהן גדול) does not come to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out a detail in the ברייתא from the last step. When the כהן גדול is the mourner, the משוח שעבר does not come to comfort him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When the כהן גדול comforts others, the ברייתא puts the משוח שעבר at his side. When others comfort the כהן גדול, the משוח שעבר is not mentioned. The גמרא reads that silence as a rule: he does not come at all.

keyTerms.meaning: A former כהן גדול who once served but no longer does

phrases.english: But the former anointed High Priest
does not come to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲבָל מָשׁוּחַ שֶׁעָבַר לָא אָתֵי גַּבֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a conclusion from what the ברייתא in step 11 leaves out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משוח שעבר does not come to comfort the mourning כהן גדול.

steps.title: Why does he not come?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the former כהן גדול stays away.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the reason?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a simple question to set up the next step: why should the משוח שעבר not come to comfort?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Comforting a mourner is normally a good deed. So it is surprising that this one person is left out, and the גמרא wants the reason.

phrases.english: What is the reason?

steps.triggerLanguage: מַאי טַעְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the inference in step 12.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the משוח שעבר does not come to comfort the כהן גדול.

steps.title: The mourner would feel his rival is gloating
steps.stepSummary: The mourning כהן גדול would feel hurt. He might think the former כהן גדול is glad about his loss.
steps.simpleTranslation: His mind would be upset. He would think: he is happy about my trouble.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers that the mourning כהן גדול would feel bad. He would think the former כהן גדול is secretly happy about what happened to him.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two men hold, or once held, the same high position, so there may be a feeling of rivalry. A visit from that person could feel like gloating instead of comfort. So the rule spares the mourner that pain.

keyTerms.meaning: His mind becomes weak, meaning he feels hurt and upset

phrases.english: His mind would become upset.
He would think: he is happy about me.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָלְשָׁא דַּעְתֵּיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 13.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mourner would feel hurt, thinking the former כהן גדול is glad about his loss.

steps.title: רב פפא learns three lessons from the ברייתא
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא draws three lessons from the ברייתא. The סגן is the same as the ממונה. Mourners stand while everyone else passes by. Mourners stand to the left of the comforters.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Learn three things from this ברייתא. First, the סגן is the same as the ממונה. Second, the mourners stand and all the people pass by. Third, the mourners stand to the left of the comforters.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא sums up three practical lessons that come out of the ברייתא about comforting the כהן גדול.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה called the helper of the כהן גדול the ממונה, and the ברייתא calls him the סגן. Since both describe the same job, they must be the same person. The ברייתא's picture of the scene also shows two customs: mourners stand still while people pass by them, and the mourners stand on the comforters' left.

keyTerms.meaning: The deputy of the כהן גדול
The appointed one; the title used in the משנה

steps.whatToRemember: From the ברייתא we learn three things: סגן and ממונה are one person, mourners stand while the people pass by, and mourners stand to the left of the comforters.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
Learn from this baraita three things.

phrases.aramaic: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ: הַיְינוּ סְגַן הַיְינוּ מְמוּנֶּה,
phrases.english: Learn from it: the deputy is the same as the appointed one,
and learn from it: mourners stand
and all the people pass by,
and learn from it: mourners, to the left
of the comforters they stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב פָּפָּא: שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ מֵהָא מַתְנִיתָא תְּלָת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sums up what can be learned from the ברייתא of step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: סגן equals ממונה; mourners stand and the people pass by; mourners stand to the left of the comforters.

steps.title: Fighting families change the order of comforting
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reports that mourners used to stand while people passed by. Two families in ירושלים fought over who would pass first, so the חכמים reversed it: the people stand and the mourners pass by.
steps.simpleTranslation: The חכמים taught: At first, mourners would stand and all the people would pass by. Two families in ירושלים fought with each other. Each one said, 'We pass first.' So the חכמים made a new rule that the people stand and the mourners pass by.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא showing that the custom רב פפא just described was later changed in ירושלים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The old way led to fights over honor: which family gets to pass the mourners first. Once the people stand still and the mourners walk past them, nobody has a place in line to fight over. A תקנה was made to keep the peace.

keyTerms.meaning: They made a new rule (a תקנה)

phrases.english: The Sages taught:
At first, the mourners would stand,
and all the people would pass by.
And there were two families in Jerusalem
fighting with each other,
this one would say: 'I pass first,'
and that one would say: 'I pass first.'
They decreed that the people should stand
and the mourners pass by.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: בָּרִאשׁוֹנָה הָיוּ אֲבֵלִים עוֹמְדִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that the custom from רב פפא's second lesson was later changed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: To stop fights, the חכמים ruled that the people stand and the mourners pass by.

steps.title: A memory aid for the next three rulings
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא gives three key words to help remember the three rulings of רבי יוסי that come next.
steps.simpleTranslation: Returned, and walk, and converse. This is a memory aid.
steps.whatsHappening: This is not an argument. The גמרא gives a memory aid to set up the three statements that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each word points to one coming ruling. 'Returned' is רבי יוסי bringing back the old custom. 'Walk' is the woman walking in the market. 'Converse' is women talking in the bathroom.

phrases.english: (Returned, and walk, and converse. A mnemonic.)
phrases.notes: These words are just a memory aid for the three rulings coming up. Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

steps.triggerLanguage: חָזַר, וְהָלַךְ, וְסִיפֵּר. סִימָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A transition that previews the three statements of רמי בר אבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A memory aid for the three תקנות of רבי יוסי.

steps.title: רבי יוסי brings back the old custom in ציפורי
steps.stepSummary: רמי בר אבא reports that רבי יוסי brought back the original custom in ציפורי: mourners stand and the people pass by.
steps.simpleTranslation: רמי בר אבא said: רבי יוסי brought the matter back to its old way in ציפורי, so that the mourners stand and all the people pass by.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reports that in his city, ציפורי, רבי יוסי went back to the original way of comforting mourners.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The change in ירושלים was made because of family fights there. In ציפורי, רבי יוסי brought back the first custom, which is also the one רב פפא learned from the ברייתא.

keyTerms.meaning: ציפורי, the city of רבי יוסי

phrases.english: Rami bar Abba said:
Rabbi Yosei returned the matter
to its old way in Tzippori,
that the mourners would stand
and all the people would pass by.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא: הֶחְזִיר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי אֶת הַדָּבָר לְיוֹשְׁנוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Reports that the ירושלים change of step 16 was reversed in ציפורי.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In ציפורי, mourners stand and the people pass by, as in the original custom.

steps.title: A son should not walk behind his mother in the market
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ruled in ציפורי that a woman should not walk in the market with her son behind her, because of something bad that once happened.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רמי בר אבא said: רבי יוסי made a rule in ציפורי that a woman should not walk in the market with her son behind her, because of something that happened.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the second תקנה of רבי יוסי: a mother should not let her son walk behind her in the market.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule was made because of a real event. A child walking behind his mother can be taken without her noticing. The rule keeps the child in front, where she can see him.

keyTerms.meaning: Because of an event that happened

phrases.english: And Rami bar Abba said:
Rabbi Yosei instituted in Tzippori
that a woman should not walk in the market
with her son behind her,
because of an incident that happened.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא: הִתְקִין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּצִיפּוֹרִי שֶׁלֹּא תְּהֵא אִשָּׁה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The second of three תקנות of רבי יוסי reported by רמי בר אבא.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A woman should not walk in the market with her son behind her.

steps.title: Women should talk in the bathroom to prevent being alone with a man
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוסי ruled in ציפורי that women should talk to each other in the bathroom, to guard against יחוד.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רמי בר אבא said: רבי יוסי made a rule in ציפורי that women should talk with each other in the bathroom, because of the concern of being alone with a man.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings the third and last תקנה of רבי יוסי: women should talk out loud in the bathroom.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The talking shows that other women are there. A man who might come in would know a woman is not alone and would stay away. This protects women from יחוד.

keyTerms.meaning: A man and woman being alone together in a private place

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יוסי made three תקנות in ציפורי. He brought back the old custom of mourners standing, made sure a son walks ahead of his mother in the market, and had women talk in the bathroom to prevent יחוד.

phrases.english: And Rami bar Abba said:
Rabbi Yosei instituted in Tzippori
that women should converse in the bathroom,
because of seclusion.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאָמַר רָמֵי בַּר אַבָּא: הִתְקִין רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּצִיפּוֹרִי שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נָשִׁים מְסַפְּרוֹת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The third and last תקנה of רבי יוסי in the series.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Women should talk in the bathroom to prevent יחוד.

steps.title: The comforters' line needs at least ten people
steps.stepSummary: רב מנשיא בר עות reports that רבי יאשיה רבה taught him that a line of comforters needs at least ten people, not counting the mourners. This applies under either custom of who stands and who passes.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב מנשיא בר עות said: I asked רבי יאשיה רבה in the cemetery of הוצל, and he told me: a line has no fewer than ten people, and the mourners are not counted. This is true whether the mourners stand and the people pass, or the mourners pass and the people stand.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא adds one more rule about the line of comforters: the minimum number of people needed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps argued about who stands and who walks. This rule sets a minimum of ten comforters, and the mourners themselves are not part of that ten. The number stays the same under both customs.

keyTerms.meaning: The line of people who comfort mourners

phrases.english: Rav Menashya bar Ute said:
I asked Rabbi Yoshiya the Great
in the cemetery of Huzal,
and he said to me:

phrases.aramaic: אֵין שׁוּרָה פְּחוּתָה מֵעֲשָׂרָה בְּנֵי אָדָם,
phrases.english: There is no line with fewer than ten people,
and the mourners are not part of the count.

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁאֲבֵלִים עוֹמְדִין וְכׇל הָעָם עוֹבְרִין,
phrases.english: whether the mourners stand and all the people pass by,

phrases.aramaic: בֵּין שֶׁאֲבֵלִים עוֹבְרִין וְכׇל הָעָם עוֹמְדִין.
phrases.english: or the mourners pass by and all the people stand.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב מְנַשְּׁיָא בַּר עוּת שְׁאֵילִית אֶת רַבִּי יֹאשִׁיָּה רַבָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a minimum number to the line-of-comforters discussion from steps 16-18.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A comforters' line needs at least ten people, not counting the mourners, under either custom.

steps.title: What does the כהן גדול say when he comforts others?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא goes back to the משנה about the כהן גדול being comforted, and asks what he says when he is the one comforting others.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'When he is comforted, etc.' A question was asked: when he comforts others, what does he say to them?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the משנה and asks a new question that the משנה did not answer. This sets up the proof that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה gave the words only for the case where the כהן גדול is being comforted: the people say 'we are your atonement' and he blesses them. For the case where he comforts others, it described only how people line up, not what words he says.

keyTerms.meaning: A question was raised before them

phrases.english: "When he is comforted, etc."
A question was asked of them:
When he comforts others,
what does he say to them?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ כִּי מְנַחֵם הוּא אַחֲרִינֵי הֵיכִי אָמַר לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the משנה and opens a new question about the כהן גדול.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The words the כהן גדול uses when he comforts other mourners.

steps.title: A ברייתא: he says 'תתנחמו'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that says the כהן גדול says 'תתנחמו', meaning 'may you be comforted'.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear: 'And he says: May you be comforted.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a source to answer the question, but it is not yet clear which situation the source is talking about.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא says the כהן גדול says 'תתנחמו', but it doesn't say whether he says it when he is being comforted or when he is comforting others. The next step works that out.

phrases.english: Come and hear:
And he says: May you be comforted.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע וְהוּא אוֹמֵר תִּתְנַחֲמוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a source to answer the question in step 22.
steps.raayaObject: What the כהן גדול says when he comforts others

steps.title: He can't be saying it to his own comforters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case the ברייתא means. It can't mean he says 'תתנחמו' to the people comforting him, because that would wish sorrow on them.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say that when others comfort him he tells them 'may you be comforted', he would be throwing a bad omen at them!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tests one possible reading of the ברייתא and rejects it. This prepares for the correct reading in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Telling the people comforting you 'may you be comforted' hints that they will also have a death and need comforting. That would be like cursing them, so the ברייתא can't mean that case.

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say: when others comfort him,
he says to them, 'May you be comforted'?
He would be throwing a bad omen at them!

steps.triggerLanguage: הֵיכִי דָמֵי אִילֵּימָא כִּי מְנַחֲמִי אַחֲרִינֵי לְדִידֵיהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects one way of reading the ברייתא from step 23.
steps.kashyaTarget: Reading the ברייתא as the כהן גדול speaking to his own comforters
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Saying 'תתנחמו' to your comforters would wish mourning on them.

steps.title: He says 'תתנחמו' when he comforts others
steps.stepSummary: So the ברייתא must mean that the כהן גדול says 'תתנחמו' when he comforts others. This answers the question.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when he comforts others he says to them 'may you be comforted'. Learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא takes the only reading left and uses it to settle the question from step 22.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading was ruled out, so the ברייתא must be describing the כהן גדול comforting others. That gives a direct answer: his words are 'תתנחמו'.

keyTerms.meaning: Learn from it, the question is settled

steps.whatToRemember: When the כהן גדול comforts other mourners, he says 'תתנחמו'.

phrases.english: Rather, when he comforts others,
he says to them, 'May you be comforted.'
Learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא כִּי מְנַחֵם לְאַחֲרִינֵי אֲמַר לְהוּ תִּתְנַחֲמוּ שְׁמַע מִינַּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct reading after step 24 rejected the other one.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The כהן גדול says 'תתנחמו' when he comforts others.

steps.title: Kings of בית דוד do judge and are judged
steps.stepSummary: On the משנה's rule that a king does not judge and is not judged, רב יוסף says it applies only to the kings of ישראל. Kings of בית דוד judge and are judged, as a פסוק commands them to do justice.
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה said: 'A king does not judge, etc.' רב יוסף said: this was taught only about the kings of ישראל. But kings of בית דוד judge and are judged, as it is written: 'House of David, so says ה׳: Do justice in the morning.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, and רב יוסף limits it to only some kings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The משנה sounded like it covered every king. רב יוסף says it only covers the kings of ישראל. Kings of בית דוד are commanded in the פסוק to judge, so they do judge.

keyTerms.meaning: They taught this only about, a phrase that limits a rule
Kings from the family of דוד
Kings not from בית דוד, such as ינאי

steps.confusionAlert: 'מלכי ישראל' here does not mean every Jewish king. It means kings who are not from בית דוד. The story the גמרא tells next is about ינאי, a king who was not from בית דוד.

phrases.english: "A king does not judge, etc."
Rav Yosef said:
They taught this only about the kings of Israel,
but the kings of the house of David
judge, and they are judged,
as it is written:
"House of David, so says ה׳:
Do justice in the morning."

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב יוֹסֵף לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new line of the משנה, about kings.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The rule that a king neither judges nor is judged applies only to kings of ישראל. Kings of בית דוד do both.
steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the contrast between the two kinds of kings for the rest of the sugya.

steps.title: Whoever judges must also be judged
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains how we know kings of בית דוד are also judged. Someone who is not judged may not judge others, as ריש לקיש learns from a פסוק: fix yourself first, then fix others.
steps.simpleTranslation: If we didn't judge him, how could he judge? But it is written: 'Gather yourselves and gather,' and ריש לקיש said: fix yourself first, and afterward fix others.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows why the פסוק about judging also proves that the king is judged.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in ירמיהו only says the king judges. But ריש לקיש teaches that a person must fix himself before he corrects others. So a king who judges others must himself be open to judgment.

keyTerms.meaning: A פסוק that ריש לקיש reads as 'fix yourselves and fix others'

phrases.english: And if we don't judge him,
how can they judge?
But isn't it written: "Gather yourselves and gather"?
phrases.notes: צפניה 2:1. ריש לקיש hears in these words the word קשט, to fix or straighten.

phrases.english: And Reish Lakish said:
Fix yourself
and afterward fix others.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאִי לָא דָּיְינִינַן לֵיהּ אִינְהוּ הֵיכִי דָּיְינִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports the second half of רב יוסף's claim in step 26, that kings of בית דוד are also judged.
steps.raayaObject: That kings of בית דוד are also judged
steps.raayaSupportSource: צפניה 2:1 as read by ריש לקיש: fix yourself before fixing others.

steps.title: Why aren't the kings of ישראל judged?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why the kings of ישראל are not judged.
steps.simpleTranslation: But the kings of ישראל, what is the reason they do not?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks for the reason behind the first half of רב יוסף's statement. This sets up the story that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once we know kings of בית דוד are judged, we need to know why the kings of ישראל are treated differently.

phrases.english: But the kings of Israel,
what is the reason they do not?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא מַלְכֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל מַאי טַעְמָא לָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the first half of רב יוסף's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why kings of ישראל are not judged

steps.title: The story begins: ינאי המלך's slave kills a person
steps.stepSummary: The reason is an incident: ינאי המלך's slave killed someone. שמעון בן שטח urged the חכמים to judge the case, they told ינאי, and he sent the slave to them.
steps.simpleTranslation: Because of an incident that happened: King ינאי's slave killed a person. שמעון בן שטח said to the חכמים: set your eyes on him and let us judge him. They sent word to ינאי: your slave killed a person. He sent the slave to them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers with a story and starts telling it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule about kings of ישראל did not come from a פסוק. It came from something that happened. The story begins with a crime by a slave of the king, which leads the בית דין into a conflict with the king himself.

keyTerms.meaning: The leading חכם of that time

phrases.english: Because of an incident that happened,
that the slave of King Yannai killed a person.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח לַחֲכָמִים:
phrases.english: Shimon ben Shatach said to the Sages:
Set your eyes on him, and let us judge him.
They sent word to him: Your slave killed a person.
He sent the slave to them.

steps.triggerLanguage: מִשּׁוּם מַעֲשֶׂה שֶׁהָיָה דְּעַבְדֵּיהּ דְּיַנַּאי מַלְכָּא קְטַל נַפְשָׁא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 28 by beginning a story.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The rule comes from an incident involving ינאי המלך.

steps.title: The חכמים call ינאי himself to court
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים tell ינאי that he must come to court too. Just as the owner of an ox that killed must stand by his ox, the master must stand by his slave.
steps.simpleTranslation: They sent word to him: You come here too. The Torah said: 'It shall be testified against with its owner' (read here as: testimony is given in the owner's presence). Let the owner of the ox come and stand by his ox.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues: the חכמים demand that the king come to court in person.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים use the law of a killing ox, where the owner must be present, to say the master must be present at his slave's trial. This turns the case into a direct test of whether the king will stand before the בית דין.

keyTerms.meaning: Literally 'its owner was warned'; the גמרא reads it as 'testified against with its owner', meaning testimony is given in the owner's presence. The פסוק about an ox that kills

phrases.english: They sent word to him:
You come here too,
"It shall be testified against with its owner," the Torah said:
Let the owner of the ox come
and stand over his ox.

steps.triggerLanguage: שְׁלַחוּ לֵיהּ תָּא אַנְתְּ נָמֵי לְהָכָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from step 29.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Like the owner of an ox, the master must come to court for his slave's case.

steps.title: שמעון בן שטח orders the king to stand
steps.stepSummary: ינאי comes to court and sits. שמעון בן שטח tells him to stand while witnesses testify, because he is standing before הקב״ה, as the פסוק says.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came and sat down. שמעון בן שטח said to him: King ינאי, stand on your feet and let the witnesses testify against you. You are not standing before us. You are standing before the One who spoke and the world came into being, as the פסוק says: 'And the two men who have the dispute shall stand...'
steps.whatsHappening: ינאי obeys the order to come to court, but he sits down. שמעון בן שטח tells him he must stand like any other person on trial.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In step 30 the חכמים said ינאי must come to court. Now there is a second demand: in court, he must stand like everyone else. שמעון בן שטח explains that standing is not about honoring the judges. A person on trial stands before הקב״ה, and the פסוק says both sides of a case must stand.

keyTerms.meaning: And let them testify against you
The One who spoke and the world came to be (הקב״ה)

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the clash between the king and the court. That clash is the reason the גמרא gives for why kings of ישראל are not judged.

phrases.english: He came and sat down.
Shimon ben Shatach said to him:
King Yannai, stand on your feet
and let them testify against you.
And it is not before us that you are standing,

phrases.aramaic: אֶלָּא לִפְנֵי מִי שֶׁאָמַר וְהָיָה הָעוֹלָם אַתָּה עוֹמֵד,
phrases.english: but before the One who spoke and the world came into being you are standing,
as it is said: "And the two men shall stand
who have the dispute, etc."
phrases.notes: דברים 19:17. The rest of the פסוק says they stand "before ה'."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲתָא וִיתֵיב. אֲמַר לֵיהּ שִׁמְעוֹן בֶּן שָׁטַח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story. After ינאי is told to come to court, he arrives, and שמעון בן שטח now demands that he stand.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A person on trial must stand while witnesses testify, because he stands before הקב״ה. This applies even to a king.

steps.title: ינאי refuses unless the other judges agree
steps.stepSummary: ינאי answers that he will not stand just because שמעון בן שטח says so. He will only follow what the other judges say.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Not as you say, but as your colleagues say.
steps.whatsHappening: ינאי refuses the order and challenges שמעון בן שטח to get the rest of the judges to back him up. This sets up the next part of the story, where we see how the other judges respond.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ינאי does not argue with the פסוק. Instead, he questions whether שמעון בן שטח alone has the authority to give the order. If the whole court agrees, he will stand. This puts the other judges to the test.

phrases.english: He said to him: Not as you say,
phrases.notes: ינאי is speaking: I won't stand just because you alone tell me to.

phrases.english: but according to what your colleagues say.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר לוֹ: לֹא כְּשֶׁתֹּאמַר אַתָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The king answers שמעון בן שטח's order from step 31 by refusing it and turning the question over to the other judges.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ינאי will only accept the order to stand if the whole court backs it, not if שמעון בן שטח says it alone.
